summary: Lighthouse on Balaklava Island at the mouth of Christie Passage, B.C.: lit April 1905; the 1905 building was replaced in 1965; still staffed by Coast Guard keepers.

corrections.why: The 1905 building was demolished in 1965 (LF); the standing round steel tower dates from the 1965 replacement. The record's tower (11.0 m, built 1905, standing) mixes the two. The 11.0 m height is not in any source read.
The 1965 Wikidata event is the replacement, not a first lighting. The light was first lit 12 April 1905 (Department). Remove the 1965 first_lit event or relabel it as the replacement.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikidata's first year 1965 is the present steel tower (the 1905 building was demolished that year). The Department's report gives 12 April 1905 as the first lighting.
Wikidata lists the light as inactive; the Coast Guard list gives Fl W 5s active, and Lighthouse Friends lists keepers to 2024.
The 1905 light was a fixed red seventh-order light; the present light flashes white every five seconds (CCG).

resolved_conflicts.field: wrecks Clara C date and pickup
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Astoria dispatch (datelined Vancouver, 22 April 1908) says the schooner blew up 'on Sunday', read here as 19 April, and that the men were picked up 'the next day'. Lighthouse Friends dates the explosion to the evening of 20 April and says the pickup came 'a few days later'. The story states both.

resolved_conflicts.field: distance and position of Balaklava Island
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends' text puts Balaklava Island about 21 km (13 miles) northwest of Port Hardy; its map caption gives about 15 km (10 miles). Its text and the 1905 report give the light on the northwest point; the map caption says northeastern point. The story gives no distance and follows the text for the point.

notes_for_editor: Keeper names and years for 1905-1939 come from Lighthouse Friends' head-keeper list, checked against three Department keeper tables: the 1907 list (Davies at scan 155, Nelson at scan 156; the footnote now gives both pages), and the 1912 list (W. Hunt, scan 81). These were matched by column position in the OCR; the page images could not be opened from the review session, so the matches rest on the OCR text. Clara C: see resolved_conflicts for the date and the pickup. The Astoria dispatch does not mention boats; Lighthouse Friends' 'two fishing dories' is cited to Lighthouse Friends. The 1916 Scandinavian grounding is in Lighthouse Friends only; the Department's 1916 wreck list was not searched for it. The Leebro account is for the fiscal year ended 31 March 1916, so the 21 July sailing is July 1915. The record's 11.0 m tower height is not in any source read. Ivan Dubinski's lottery story in Lighthouse Friends is left out as personal and irrelevant. Keepers after 1960 are named only as the published list prints them. Vivian Hunt's private family details are reduced to what the story needs.
